nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
ESFLOT

Several waves of rain, and possibly a few thunderstorms, are likely
through Thursday night. High moisture content in the atmosphere will
lead to periods of torrential downpours and the threat for 1 to 3
inches of rainfall on a widespread basis through Thursday night.

Repeated rounds of rain over saturated soils may lead to flooding of
low-lying and poor drainage areas as well as rises on area rivers,
including along the Rock, Fox, DuPage, Des Plaines, and Illinois
Rivers.

This outlook means that elevated water levels and potential impacts
are possible, but not yet certain. Persons should closely monitor
forecasts including the possibility of flood watches, warnings, and
advisories.

Additional statements or outlooks may be issued by this afternoon.

FXUS63 KIWX 301013
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
613 AM EDT Wed Sep 30 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Increasing chances (40-80%) for showers today along and mainly
  north of US 24 , best potential will remain near Lake MI in 
  the mid-late afternoon. Highs will be in the upper 60s, low 
  70s for those areas. South of US 24 expect highs in the mid-
  upper 70s with increasing clouds. 

- Rain chances (40-90%) spread eastward through Friday, with 
  isolated thunderstorm potential (non-severe). Highs will be in
  the 70s, low 80s on Thursday and the 60s Friday. 

- Dry conditions are expected this weekend into early next 
  week, with highs in the 60s, low 70s (warmest further south). 
  Overnight lows will drop into the 40s.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 345 AM EDT Wed Sep 30 2026

Not a whole lot of changes to the going forecast. Rain showers 
continue over northern IL into central MI this morning with the
band of showers on the northwest periphery of ridging further 
south and east which will mainly keep the introduction of rain 
showers for areas closer to Lake Michigan into this afternoon 
as the lower levels further moisten. WPC has a marginal risk for
excessive rainfall for later today and as the ridging pushes 
further south and east rain showers will make their way further 
south and east through Friday morning with a slight risk for 
excessive rainfall for tomorrow. A few embedded thunderstorms 
will be possible with the southern and eastward push but at this
time severe weather is not anticipated. 

A more zonal aloft pattern emerges across the region this
weekend and will bring a return to dry conditions and cooler
temperatures especially into the beginning of next week when
highs will only get to around 60 degrees both Monday and
Tuesday.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 611 AM EDT Wed Sep 30 2026

Light rain showers currently observed on latest radar imagery
starting to push into northwest IN with some of the showers
making it to the surface. These showers are on the 
northwestern periphery of ridging in place further south and 
east. Showers look to remain light as the showers push further 
southward over mainly areas near Lake Michigan and into KSBN, so
at this time think conditions will mainly remain VFR however 
some slight reductions in vsbys due to rain showers may allow 
for MVFR vsbys but at this time confidence remains low. At this 
time KFWA looks to remain dry with the ridging in place over 
south and eastern portions of the CWA.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Andersen
AVIATION...Andersen

spc.text:
SPC AC 300553

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1253 AM CDT Wed Sep 30 2026

   Valid 301200Z - 011200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM SOUTHWEST
   OK/NORTHWEST TX INTO THE EDWARDS PLATEAU...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms capable of severe wind gusts and possibly a brief
   tornado appear possible across portions of the southern Plains this
   afternoon into tonight. A conditional risk for isolated severe wind
   gusts and perhaps a couple tornadoes exists over parts of Kansas and
   southern Nebraska this afternoon and evening.

   ...Central/southern Plains...
   A mid/upper-level low will move from the southern Rockies toward the
   central High Plains through the period. A surface low initially over
   the southern High Plains is forecast to move only slowly eastward
   into tonight. A warm front extending northeast of the surface low
   may move slowly northward through the day, though persistent clouds
   and precipitation may slow its advance. 

   A rather strong low-level jet is forecast to slowly shift
   northeastward across parts of central/eastern KS into western MO and
   southeast NE/southwest IA later today into the evening. This will
   help to maintain favorable wind profiles in the vicinity of the
   effective warm front. Destabilization near the warm front may remain
   weak due to limited diurnal heating and weak midlevel lapse rates.
   However, if sufficient buoyancy can develop by late afternoon, there
   will be potential for surface-based supercell development, which
   could pose a localized tornado and damaging-wind threat. 

   Farther south, the coverage and persistence of early-day convection
   across the southern Plains remain somewhat uncertain, though there
   may be a tendency for convection to weaken and/or shift northward by
   early afternoon. The greatest confidence in substantial diurnal
   destabilization is from southwest OK into northwest TX and the
   Edwards Plateau, where heating of a very moist airmass will result
   in MLCAPE increasing to near/above 1500 J/kg, despite poor midlevel
   lapse rates. Renewed storm development is expected from late
   afternoon into the evening, in advance of the approaching
   mid/upper-level low. Moderate midlevel flow will provide sufficient
   deep-layer shear for storm organization. 

   While supercells will be possible initially, generally
   front-parallel flow and increasing storm coverage will likely lead
   to more of a linear mode with time. Strong to severe gusts appear to
   be the most likely hazard, though isolated hail also appears
   possible across southwest TX, where somewhat stronger
   destabilization may occur. Also, while low-level flow will be weaker
   compared to areas farther north, some increase in effective SRH is
   expected during the evening, which could support a localized brief
   tornado threat within the very moist environment. 

   An isolated severe threat could persist into parts of central TX/OK
   overnight, though diminishing buoyancy with time and eastward extent
   should result in an eventual weakening trend.

   ..Dean/Weinman.. 09/30/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.summary: Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts will be possible on Thursday across parts of the southern Plains.
spc.text:
SPC AC 300541

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1241 AM CDT Wed Sep 30 2026

   Valid 011200Z - 021200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   THE SOUTHERN PLAINS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts will be possible on
   Thursday across parts of the southern Plains.

   ...Southern Plains...
   A positively-tilted mid-level shortwave trough will move
   northeastward across the southern Plains on Thursday. At the
   surface, a cold front will advance south-southeastward across
   Oklahoma and west Texas. Ahead of the front, surface dewpoints from
   the mid 60s to lower 70s F will contribute to destabilization along
   a corridor from central Texas north-northeastward into eastern
   Oklahoma. As surface temperatures warm, isolated to scattered
   thunderstorms will possible along and near the instability axis in
   areas where low-level convergence becomes maximized. By mid to late
   afternoon, steepening low-level lapse rates will make isolated
   severe wind gusts a possibility. This threat could continue into the
   early evening as low-level flow increases. Any wind-damage threat
   that develops is expected to remain marginal.

   ..Broyles.. 09/30/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 300718

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0218 AM CDT Wed Sep 30 2026

   Valid 021200Z - 031200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are expected across the U.S. on Friday.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   A mid-level trough over the Ozarks Friday morning is forecast to
   weaken and move east-northeastward into the Ohio Valley. At the
   surface, a cold front is forecast to advance southeastward into the
   lower Mississippi and Tennessee Valleys. Along and to the south of
   the front, isolated to scattered thunderstorms may develop in areas
   where instability and low-level convergence become maximized during
   the afternoon. Over the moist airmass, the combination of
   instability and deep-layer shear is expected to be insufficient for
   a severe threat.

   ..Broyles.. 09/30/2026
